misconception_description: Student believes that loop variables are destroyed and are inaccessible after the loop completes.

solutions.generated_code:
program PalindromBerikutnya
kamus
  n, kandidat, sisa, hasilBalik, ketemu : integer
  sudahKetemu : boolean
algoritma
  input(n)
  kandidat <- n + 1
  sudahKetemu <- false
  ketemu <- 0
  while not sudahKetemu do
    sisa <- kandidat
    hasilBalik <- 0
    while sisa > 0 do
      hasilBalik <- hasilBalik * 10 + (sisa mod 10)
      sisa <- sisa div 10
    endwhile
    if hasilBalik == kandidat then
      ketemu <- kandidat
      sudahKetemu <- true
    else
      kandidat <- kandidat + 1
    endif
  endwhile
  output(ketemu)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student believes that loop variable 'i' is destroyed after the loop completes, so they create a separate variable 'found_palindrome' to store the palindrome value during the loop iteration. Instead of simply returning 'i' after breaking from the loop (or returning directly inside the loop), they store it in 'found_palindrome' and return that variable instead. This is unnecessary but doesn't cause any bugs - the code still works correctly. The student genuinely believes this is the proper way to preserve the value since they think 'i' won't exist after the loop ends.
